title: Orion BioSearch — relevance API + reranker hosted walkthrough
summary: Hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranking workflow for biomedical search. Demo showed embeddings endpoint, approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) integration, and server-side reranker using Redwood hosted rerank endpoint. Customer concerned about latency at tail, data residency, and pilot benchmark scope. Agreed next steps: share security pack, pricing estimate for 50 qps pilot, and kickoff benchmark run next week.
next_steps: Redwood: send SOC2 / security packet + KMS integration notes (Sophie)
Redwood: pricing for 50 qps pilot + dedicated capacity options (Sophie)
Customer: provide sample dataset excerpt and relevance test queries (Ravi)
Schedule pilot kickoff + benchmark slot next Tuesday 10am PT

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-18 15:00 UTC — Duration ~62m — Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Ivy (notes), Emily (Orion Head Search), Ravi (ML), Jenna (SRE), Noah (PM)

[00:00] Sophie: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll spend most of the time on the hosted embeddings + reranker flow, quick intros?
[00:12] Emily: hi I'm Emily head of search at Orion BioSearch, thanks for making time.
[00:15] Ravi: Ravi here, I'm the ML lead building our vector search pipeline. we've been prototyping with Milvus and a homegrown reranker.
[00:21] Sophie: great, and Marco is our SE who'll demo the flow and show the console insights, Ivy will capture notes.
[00:28] Marco: hi all, i'll share my screen in a sec, but quick agenda: embeddings endpoint, ANN integration patterns, server-side reranker API, console observability, and a short Optimize recommendations run (batching/quant).
[00:39] Noah: quick ask — our docs are biomedical, a lot of PII-ish material, we need to confirm data residency and KMS support.
[00:46] Jenna: and we care about tail latency — 99th percentile under load, because clinicians depend on sub-second responses.
[00:52] Marco: understood. we support SOC2, customer-managed KMS via HSM or cloud KMS, and we can run private deployments if required; hosted has region-level data residency options.
[01:05] Sophie: i'm noting security pack and KMS notes as an action item.
[01:12] Marco: ok i'm sharing the console now — apologies if screen glints. starting with embeddings endpoint: you POST documents, we return embeddings vectors, can also do batched uploads. most folks store vectors in their ANN store (we integrate with common stores — you can use Milvus, Pinecone, or self-hosted Faiss).
[01:32] Emily: does Redwood host the index or do we always push to our own vector DB?
[01:36] Marco: you can do either. for a quick pilot the common path is: Redwood hosted embeddings API -> push vectors to your existing ANN (e.g., Milvus) -> on query, run ANN retrieval client-side then call our reranker endpoint for re-ranking top k. alternatively we offer an internal vector store integration where we manage the index for you and handle the ANN step server-side, which simplifies ops.
[01:58] Ravi: when you say "reranker endpoint" is that model-in-the-loop hosted by Redwood? how much control do we have over the rerank model and prompts?
[02:05] Marco: yes, it's hosted. you can pick verified rerank model flavors, pin model versions, and supply structured scoring prompts; we also support function/tool calling style structured outputs. prompts are passed as part of the rerank request so you can iterate quickly.
[02:20] Sophie: i'll add a note: demo will show the live rerank call with our default biomedical-tuned reranker.

[02:32] [02:32] Marco: ok demo time — first I'll run a small end-to-end local query: POST to /embeddings with sample doc, store vector in Milvus, run ANN search, then call /rerank with top 50 and show delta in relevance.
[02:47] Marco: (typing) the embed endpoint accepts text, optional metadata; we see the vector payload come back, then we call our server-side rerank: body contains candidate IDs, query text, structured prompt.
[03:12] (audio hiss)
[03:18] Emily: can you show latencies? even off demo network numbers help.
[03:21] Marco: sure, here's the timeline — embed 120ms, ANN lookup 30ms, reranker 240ms, total ~390ms for this sample. under load those numbers rise, but our continuous batching and K V cache — um kv cache — reduces repeated context cost.
[03:42] Ravi: 240ms for rerank, what model size is that? is it quantized?
[03:47] Marco: this was a medium reranker variant, quantized int8 for inference. for tighter latency we can use a smaller reranker or apply progressive reranking: lightweight lexical + small rerank model on the first cut, heavy pass async.
[04:05] Jenna: how do fallbacks work if the host region is saturated? we need graceful degradation.
[04:10] Marco: smart routing — requests route by policy; you can configure fallback to a cheaper model variant or to a different region. the console shows per-route SLOs and automatic fallback counts.

[04:28] Sophie: quick pivot to costs — most customers using hosted embeddings + rerank see two levers: tune top-k and rerank model size. Marco, can you show Optimize recommendations?
[04:38] Marco: jumping to Optimize — it runs on workload traces and suggests batching thresholds, cache TTL for prefixes, and recommends model quantization profiles. here's a sample suggestion: for your workload shape (median query length ~12 tokens), use batch size 8 for embed ingestion and prefer q4_0 quant for reranker to save ~35% token cost with negligible quality loss on held-out prompts.
[05:02] Ravi: interesting, do you have metrics from a biomedical workload? sometimes distillation hurts our domain-specific synonyms.
[05:09] Marco: we keep per-prompt evals — we can run a relevance eval against your 1k queries and produce an A/B between model variants. i'll flag that as a bench item.

[05:20] [05:20] Emily: security — can you confirm logs and audit trail retention? our compliance team wants immutable audit logs for 7 years ideally.
[05:28] Marco: hosted console provides audit logs and trace exports to your SIEM; retention is configurable as an add-on. long-term archival we can push to your S3 with WORM policies if needed. SOC2 cert included in the security packet.

[05:42] Noah: regarding data residency — our corp policy requires data at rest for vectors to be in eu-west-1 for EU patients. what are options?
[05:50] Sophie: hosted region selection is possible and we can also do private deployment (VPC / on-prem) if isolation is required. again, we'll include region and private deployment notes in the security pack.

[06:05] Marco: back to the demo — i'm going to show the console trace for a query at 50 qps sustained in a test. notice the token-level breakdown, rerank time, and cache hits. (screen) you can filter to per-route metrics and see cost per 1k requests.
[06:28] Jenna: that token-level billing is helpful. any way to map that to our cardinal cost lines?
[06:32] Marco: yes the console can export per-route cost CSVs. for pilot sizing we do an estimate based on embed ingestion, vector store calls, and reranker token charges.

[06:45] Ravi: question on consistency — our results depend on deterministic reranks for reproducibility in audits. is there nondeterministic output?
[06:52] Marco: outputs can be deterministic if you pin model version and set sampling to deterministic. there are some nondet ops for sampling-based flows but rerank is typically deterministic by default if you use scoring prompts.

[07:05] Emily: ok timeline — we want a 3-week pilot: week 1 ingest ~200k docs, week 2 run A/B relevance benchmark at 50 qps, week 3 integrate into staging and measure 99th pct latency. do you support that cadence?
[07:17] Sophie: yes that's feasible. our recommendation is start with hosted embeddings + push to your Milvus (you keep vector control), then use Redwood rerank endpoint for scoring so we can measure improvements quickly.
[07:28] Marco: for the benchmark we'll instrument our bench harness — i'll share the script and the spreadsheet template.

[07:35] Ravi: what's the cost ballpark for 50 qps pilot — say sustained 50 qps for a week with rerank on top 50?
[07:42] Sophie: i'll put together pricing but back-of-envelope: embedding ingestion cost + reranker per-call token cost. for that scale we often recommend a small dedicated pool to stabilize latency, but we can do hosted first; i'll include both hosted estimate and dedicated reserved pricing.

[07:58] [07:58] Marco: quick deep dive — integration code example: we showed node/python snippets. you call /v1/embeddings -> push vectors -> on query do ANN search -> call /v1/rerank with candidates. rerank request example includes candidate metadata which we use for context scoring.
[08:18] Ravi: do you accept chunked docs and per-chunk metadata? we chunk pubmed abstracts heavily.
[08:23] Marco: yes, chunking is common. we recommend storing chunk ids and source doc metadata so rerank can penalize duplicates and boost recency.

[08:34] Emily: on-model governance — can we run A/B where one arm uses our in-house fine-tuned reranker?
[08:40] Marco: we support hybrid: you can host your reranker in your infra and call it in the loop, or route the top-k through our hosted reranker. either way, the console will capture end-to-end traces for comparison.

[08:52] Jenna: any network egress concerns? pushing vectors to our Milvus will leave vectors in our network, but rerank calls to Redwood mean query text leaves our VPC.
[08:59] Sophie: for sensitive data you can sanitize text client-side or run Private (VPC) deployment where the control plane is customer-managed and data doesn't leave the VPC. we'll document options.

[09:12] Marco: demo wrap-up — here's the rerank delta: baseline lexical score vs reranked top results, and you can see precision@5 improves from .62 to .82 on this sample set. caveats: sample size small and domain-specific synonyms vary.
[09:32] Emily: would like to see that metric on our data.

[09:36] Sophie: agreed — action: Ravi shares 1k queries and labels, Marco runs an eval and returns A/B.

[09:45] (brief pause)

[09:48] Marco: quick note on batching: for embed ingestion we batch on the client side, and Redwood can also batch at the runtime with continuous batching which reduces per-token latency cost. Optimize suggested batch size 8 for your distribution.

[10:05] Ravi: curious about the kv cache — does it persist across model version rollouts? we want to avoid cold starts.
[10:11] Marco: KV cache is tied to model variant; when you rollout you can configure cache warm-up policies. and we offer automatic pre-populate hooks for known hot prefixes.

[10:24] Emily: procurement — what's typical lead time for enterprise contract once pilot completes?
[10:28] Sophie: usually 4–6 weeks for dedicated capacity deals; hosted extension can be shorter. procurement will want SAML SSO, SOC2, and DPA; we'll include templates.

[10:40] Sophie: ok let's recap and confirm next steps.
[10:42] Marco: recap: run bench on customer queries, produce A/B between model variants, share bench harness.
[10:47] Sophie: i'll send security pack (SOC2, KMS, data residency options), pricing for 50 qps pilot plus dedicated estimate, and schedule kickoff for next Tuesday 10am PT.
[10:55] Emily: sounds good. Ravi will send sample queries. Jenna will review networking options.
[11:00] Sophie: thanks all — any final q's?
[11:03] Ravi: one more, can you show the rerank request/response schema after — it's helpful for engineering?
[11:07] Marco: yes i'll paste examples in the follow-up and link to the SDK snippets.
[11:12] (wrap up, off camera goodbyes)

References shared during call: Redwood demo deck (link: https://app.redwood.ai/decks/embeddings-rerank-demo), bench spreadsheet (link: https://sheets.redwood.ai/orion-bench-template), security pack placeholder (link: https://redwood.ai/security/pack.pdf).

End transcript.
